title: Repair learner Career screen API contract and remove demo fallback

spec.problem: The active Career screen renders prototype state anonymously and crashes for authenticated users because the UI expects a nested response while Go returns a flat CareerMe record. The view also resolves rank labels from mock data.

acceptance.text: Career page consumes Go CareerMe JSON and renders persisted learner fields without fabricated NPC, skill, or rank values.
Anonymous/API failure state shows localized retry/login-safe UI and never falls back to prototype career data.
Career ranks and skills render only when supplied by backend endpoints; empty datasets have explicit empty states.
At 390x844 the page has no horizontal overflow; screen state and Career API methods/paths are checkpointed.

Partial skill datasets display only measured values; missing axes remain unavailable and incomplete data is not plotted as zero. A real-browser UI regression exercises the 390x844 layout and asserts both Career GET method/path pairs, including empty-rank messaging.
A newly created Career profile with an empty work name is eligible for the existing localized name-onboarding UI; every saved non-empty name is accepted and does not prompt again.
Saving a Career work name through the existing UI normalizes the Go flat PATCH response, updates the parent learner state, and keeps the saved name visible.

spec.expected_behavior: Authenticated learners see persisted career profile data only; absent fields show honest empty states. Anonymous or failed requests never show demo identity or progress.
spec.observed_behavior: Anonymous /vi/career displays mock rank, skill, and NPC values while /api/career/me and /api/career/ranks return 401. After visible registration, both API reads return 200 but CareerPageClient dereferences response.state although Go returns flat CareerMe, triggering the Next error boundary.
spec.rollback_plan: Revert the Career page/API adapter and tests as one commit; retain protected Go API routes and existing PostgreSQL rows.
